about: T16 captions, written as a warm, clear tutor speaking; can be recorded as voiceover later. Times in seconds from the start of the lesson.

lines.text: Lesson sixteen: trend and market structure.
We'll read the shape of price, one peak and dip at a time.
Here is a fictional BTC chart. Is price going up, down, or nowhere?
One candle cannot tell you. Look at the peaks and the dips instead.
The pattern they make is called market structure.
It describes the past. It does not promise the future.
A swing high is a peak: price rose, then turned down.
A swing low is a dip: price fell, then turned up.
Think of a hilly road. The hilltops are swing highs, the valleys swing lows.
A peak is only clear after price turns away from it.
An uptrend has higher highs and higher lows.
Each peak tops the last one: 60,100, then 60,200, then 60,300.
Each dip stays above the last one: 59,980, then 60,080, then 60,180.
Like climbing stairs: a step up, a small step back, then up again.
HH means higher high. HL means higher low.
A downtrend is the mirror: lower highs and lower lows.
Peaks: 60,320, then 60,220, then 60,120. Each one is lower.
Dips: 60,200, then 60,100, then 60,000. LH and LL for short.
Lower highs, lower lows: a downtrend, so far.
Sideways means neither: highs and lows stay at about the same levels.
Peaks near 60,200, dips near 60,000. Price moves, but goes nowhere.
This is also called a range. No clear direction is an answer too.
Now watch structure change as price writes the chart.
Higher highs, higher lows: an uptrend.
Each new label appears only after price turns. That is how swings work.
Then a peak that is not higher: the climb stalls, sideways.
A lower high, then a lower low. The structure has turned down.
Structure tells you what changed. It cannot tell you what comes next.
Let's check with numbers. Compare each peak with the last peak.
60,240 minus 60,290 is minus 50. A lower high.
60,060 minus 60,150 is minus 90. A lower low.
Both changed: the uptrend's pattern of higher highs and lows is broken.
A common mistake: one big green candle does not make an uptrend.
Here, a big jump, but the highs and lows are still falling.
Trend comes from the pattern of swings, not from one candle.
And always say which timeframe you mean.
Your turn. Three fictional charts: A, B and C.
Which is an uptrend, which a downtrend, which sideways? Pause if you need time.
A: lower highs and lower lows. A downtrend.
B: highs and lows at the same levels. Sideways.
C: higher highs and higher lows. An uptrend.
Well done if you got all three.
Be honest about the limits. Spotting swings is partly a judgement call.
Two people can mark the same chart differently, and both can be fair.
Tiny wiggles are usually ignored. A different timeframe can show a different trend.
Before we move on, a few honest limits.
A trend can end at any time, often without warning.
Buying late into a long trend can mean buying near the top.
Structure is not a signal to trade. WAIT and NO_TRADE are always allowed.
Let's recap.
Uptrend: higher highs and higher lows. Downtrend: lower highs and lower lows.
Sideways: highs and lows stay at about the same levels.
Swings are only clear after price turns, and they are a judgement call.
Check yourself: peaks 60,300 then 60,240; dips 60,150 then 60,060. What is it?
Lower highs and lower lows: a downtrend, so far.
Great work! Next up: support, resistance, breakout and fakeout.
See you in lesson seventeen.
